newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Chinese, Russian investors mull Fokker restart.
newsitem.headline: Chinese, Russian investors mull Fokker restart.

text.p: A group of Russian and Chinese investors has expressed interest in relaunching bankrupt aircraft maker Fokker and has contacted Dutch entrepreneur Rosen Jacobson who had been involved in previous Fokker rescue talks, a joint statement from the investors said.

Russian investors, united in the Interconversiya Group, and Chinese investors, under supervision of Henry Ho of the Turmile group and the Harbin Aircraft Industry Company, are interested in reviving Fokker, whose factories are mothballed.
"The question now is if the administrators agree on the refloat," said spokesman Dick Rijshouwer.

Rijshouwer, who is the spokesman for one of the enterpreneurs involved in the current talks, said that the talks were very serious and that the parties involved had been speaking about how to finance the restart.
"Money is not a problem," said Rijnshouwer. "The Chinese have plenty," he said.
The Russian and Chinese investors who have expressed interest in Fokker are expected to arrive in the Netherlands next week.

Fokker was declared bankrupt in 1996 after parent Daimler Benz cut off financial support following catastrophic losses. Since then a number of suitors have expressed interest but none have come to the company's rescue.

Earlier this year the Dutch government said it saw now further chance of restarting Fokker and the stricken plane maker's administrators said a break up and sale of the company's assets looked inevitable.
